text:
maya: Idea: tiny customer-facing prefetch widget snippet we can drop into onboarding emails. Purpose: reduce first-response jitter and capture a one-question feedback. Keep it copy-light.

ryan.cs: Nice. Keep it 3 steps max and include a privacy reassurance. Also add a small JS example for front-end teams.

emma.sre: Ops constraints: no bulk prefill, TTL <= 45m, cap qps to 0.3/account, and emit warmup metrics. If 429s happen, back off with jitter.

maya: Draft customer copy:
1) Confirm your region with your CS rep.
2) Paste this small widget into a staging page and click Run (it sends 3 tiny sample queries spaced 10s apart).
3) After 30m the system will auto-expire the prefills.

Privacy blurb: "No model training or long-term storage; this only primes caches for faster first calls."

ryan.cs: JS widget snippet (customer-facing):

```
fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer <KEY>', 'X-Prefill-TTL': '30m' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'redwood-lite-1', input: 'Short summary prompt' })
}).then(r=>console.log('prefill',r.status))
```

emma.sre: Telemetry: emit `prefetch.widget.run` + `prefetch.widget.result` with success/fail. CS dashboard card should show last_run and a yes/no feedback count (customer answered "Was the first response fast? Y/N"). If two consecutive widget runs fail, set CRM tag `widget-warmup-failed`.

product-bot: Action: add account card for widget status and feedback. Owners: cs-team, eng-platform.

maya: Final ops note: include an internal one-line rollback to clear ephemeral keys for an account: `curl -X POST https://internal.redwood.local/admin/cache/clear -d 'account_id=ACCT&scope=prefetch'`. I'll write the one-pager and post tomorrow in #customer-success for a quick review.
